body:
The SPA e2e suite began running on main pushes with #1557, and it intermittently
fails with a TRANSPORT error rather than an assertion:

    Error: apiRequestContext.post: socket hang up
      -> POST http://localhost:8083/api/v1/books/6/metadata
      at setBookTags (frontend/e2e/tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:74)

The server closed the connection mid-request. That is a finding about the app
under concurrency, not about the test.

Evidence it is load, not a broken spec:
- The same run tallies "1 failed, 364 passed" — most of the visible failures are
  RETRIES of the same two specs, and they pass on retry.
- A later main push (#1561, changelog-only) ran the identical suite green:
  E2E Tests (SPA) success, steps=21.
- Observed across tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:109/:140 (desktop),
  reader-rtl.spec.ts:90 and sp2-display-options.spec.ts:61 (mobile) — i.e. it is
  not localised to one endpoint.

Why it matters beyond the suite: e2e on main is wired to auto-revert, whose
premise is "Test Suite failed on a main push => the head commit broke it". A lane
that fails on load makes that premise false at random, so innocent commits get
reverted (already seen: #1563 reverted a docs-only commit). #1564 contains the
revert side; this finding is the underlying cause.

Worth checking whether the failure is the app (gevent worker exhaustion / a
blocking call under parallel requests — note this deployment has NO
monkey.patch_all(), so one blocking call stalls the hub) or the test harness's
server. The distinction decides whether real users hit it under concurrent load.
title: The server drops connections under parallel e2e load, failing tests transport-level
